statements.t: “We will continue to align wholesale shipments with retail demand to support our dealers through this cycle, and our outlook for the next quarter reflects that approach.

We remain intentional about our outlook until we see more durable evidence of a broader recovery, but our conviction in Build, Innovate, Grow and the mid-cycle opportunity in front of us remains strong.”
Our cash flow for the quarter reflected an uptick in normal seasonal working capital, which we expect to reverse as the year progresses.
With our $70 million share repurchase authorization in place, we will remain balanced and disciplined in allocating capital as we execute against our strategy.”
The Company expects working capital needs to decrease as the year progresses, consistent with historical seasonality patterns.
The Company’s first full fiscal year under the new reporting calendar will be the twelve months ending December 31, 2027.
The Company’s outlook for that period, issued on August 27, 2026, is therefore superseded by the outlook below.
For the three months ending December 31, 2026, the Company expects net sales of $236 million to $248 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $13.0 million to $15.0 million.
For the six-month Transition Period ending December 31, 2026, the Company expects net sales of $489 million to $501 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $27.3 million to $29.3 million.
The Company expects to provide its initial calendar year 2027 outlook in March 2027, concurrent with the reporting of its Transition Period results.
The Company has not provided reconciliations of guidance for Adjusted EBITDA, in reliance on the unreasonable efforts exception provided under Item 10(e)(1)(i)(B) of Regulation S-K.
The Company is unable, without unreasonable efforts, to forecast certain items required to develop meaningful comparable GAAP financial measures.
Our presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures should also not be construed as an inference that our results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items.

Many of these risks and uncertainties are outside our control, and there may be other risks and uncertainties which we do not currently anticipate because they relate to events and depend on circumstances that may or may not occur in the future.

our third-party suppliers' increased costs or inability to adjust for our required production levels
our dependence on a small group of suppliers for components
our ability to meet our manufacturing workforce needs
our dependence on key management employees
our growth strategy which may require us to secure significant additional capital
our ability to enhance existing products and develop and market new or enhanced products

risks and requirements related to transacting business in foreign countries

statements.t: We have maintained a disciplined approach to wholesale shipments, and we continue to expect a modest further reduction in dealer inventories during the three months ending December 31, 2026 and into 2027.

We expect retail demand to remain soft during the three months ending December 31, 2026 and into 2027 amid continued macroeconomic uncertainty, and we expect promotional activity and dealer incentive costs, including floor plan interest support, to remain elevated relative to historical levels.
We aim to increase our market share across the boating categories in which we compete through new product development, improved distribution, new models, and innovative features.
We continue to integrate Saxdor, our newest acquisition, into the business, and expected synergies have the potential to be realized over the coming years.
Our financial results and operations have been, and will continue to be, impacted by events outside of our control.
We estimate that 18-20% of our cost of sales for our brands located in the U.S. are sourced from outside the United States.

Assuming current tariff rates, we continue to expect to incur material costs through the three months ending December 31, 2026 and into 2027 from new tariff exposure of approximately 1.5% to 3% of cost of sales, including Saxdor boats shipped to the U.S.
We expect to largely offset these added costs through recent price increases.
For the three months ending December 31, 2026 and into 2027, we expect to continue to experience reduced retail consumer demand for our products and a competitive promotional environment.
However, we will maintain our disciplined approach to dealer health and leverage our strong balance sheet and cash generation to continue investing in the business.
Our unaudited interim consolidated financial results for these periods are not necessarily indicative of the consolidated financial results that we will achieve in future periods.
Our presentation of adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin should not be construed as an inference that our results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items.
Our presentation of adjusted net income per share should not be construed as an inference that our results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items.

Our acquisition of Saxdor also provides for up to €71.3 million or $84.2 million in potential earnout payments (the “earnout consideration”) to the sellers during the calendar years 2027, 2028 and 2029 based on the results of the remainder of calendar year 2026 and the subsequent two calendar years (the "earnout period"), subject to the achievement of certain specified post-closing operating and financial targets.

Under the tax receivable agreement, we pay the pre-IPO owners (or any permitted assignees) 85% of the amount of cash savings, if any, in U.S. federal, state and local income tax or franchise tax that we actually realize, or in some circumstances are deemed to realize, as a result of an expected increase in our share of tax basis in LLC’s tangible and intangible assets, including increases attributable to payments…
We estimate that approximately $0.1 million will be due under the tax receivable agreement within the next 12 months.
Our expected operating lease payments due within the next 12 months are $5.5 million and our total committed lease payments are $11.6 million as of September 30, 2026.

We intend to vigorously pursue our claims against the insurance carrier to recover the full $100.0 million settlement amount and expenses (less any monies already tendered without reservation by the carrier).
